speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; could you please describe exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain feels like pressure, burning, or sharpness?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture).

The history of forceful vomiting following alcohol consumption, followed by choking, coughing, and chest pain, is highly specific for an esophageal rupture. I will request a Chest X-Ray and a CT scan of the chest with contrast to confirm the diagnosis and check for mediastinal air or fluid.
